headline: Police vehicle vandalised, activities-banned AL leader taken away in handcuffs

members.title: Police vehicle vandalised, activities-banned AL leader taken away in handcuffs
members.lead: A group of people stopped a police vehicle in Jaintiapur, Sylhet, and snatched a leader of Awami League, whose activities are banned, while he was handcuffed. They also vandalised the police vehicle. The incident took place on Monday night in the Koricher Pul area of Haripur in the upazila of Sylhet. . Police later conducted a drive and detained three people on suspicion of involvement in the incident. The Awami League (activities banned) leader is Zakaria Mahmud from Hemu Haudpara village in the Haripur area. . He is the deputy office secretary of Jaintiapur upazila Awami League and a former joint general secretary of the district Chhatra League. According to police sources, Zakaria Mahmud was detained by police from the Station area of Haripur Bazar in Jaintiapur at around 7:30pm on Monday. . While he was being taken to the police station, several people blocked the police vehicle with a pickup truck in the Koricher Pul area of the Sylhet–Tamabil highway, about one kilometre from the market. They vandalised the police vehicle and took Zakaria away while he was still handcuffed. Jaintiapur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mahbubur Rahman Molla said five cases had been filed against Zakaria at the police station. He was detained on Monday night. While he was being taken to the police station, the police vehicle was blocked and the detainee was snatched away along with his handcuffs. Police later conducted a drive at night and detained three people involved in the incident. OC Mahbubur Rahman Molla further said that operations were underway to arrest Zakaria and the others involved in snatching him away.

members.title: Police vehicle torched, clashes in Gopalganj
members.lead: Clashes and chases took place between police and leaders and activists of the banned Chhatra League in Tungipara, Gopalganj. During the clashes, a police vehicle was set on fire and several shops were vandalised. Several people, including police personnel, were injured. Meanwhile, leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations blocked roads at different locations in Kashiani upazila by setting fires. Roads were also blocked near the western side of Launchghat Bridge, at Sonakur and at the LGED intersection in Gopalganj town. The incidents took place at various locations in Tungipara, Kashiani and Sadar upazilas from Tuesday morning. According to police and local sources, leaders and activists of the banned Chhatra League blocked a road by setting fire at Gawhardanga Chowrangi intersection in Tungipara at around 9:30am. They were later joined by leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities are banned, and its affiliate banned organisation Jubo League. . They brought out a procession from Chowrangi, passing through Patgati Bus Stand, and proceeded to Patgati Bazar. There, they vandalised several festoons and banners placed outside the Jubo Dal office. After returning to Patgati Bus Stand in a procession, they were stopped by police, triggering chases and clashes between the two sides. According to eyewitnesses, during the clashes, protesters set fire to a police vehicle on the road beside Gimadanga Tungipara High School. Several shops were also vandalised. Vehicular movement on the Gopalganj-Pirojpur road remained suspended for nearly two hours. At least 10 people, including police personnel, were injured in the clashes. They received treatment at Tungipara Upazila Health Complex and locally. Tungipara police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Ayub Ali told Prothom Alo that clashes broke out between the two sides when police tried to stop the banned Chhatra League's strike. members.title: Vehicles set on fire, crude bomb explosions: What message IGP sends to SPs
members.lead: A total of 22 vehicles were set on fire across the country in the past 24 hours. During this period, miscreants exploded crude bombs at at least 28 locations in Dhaka and six other districts. Sources at the Police Headquarters and Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) said vehicles were set on fire in 11 districts, both in and outside Dhaka. The incidents took place between Monday morning and Tuesday morning. Meanwhile, a police vehicle was set on fire, roads were blocked and shops were vandalised in Gopalganj today, Tuesday. Over the past three days, a series of acts of sabotage have been reported across the country. Against this backdrop, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir held a meeting with the superintendents of police (SPs) of all 64 districts. He instructed them to arrest those involved in sabotage, intensify patrols and strengthen intelligence surveillance. All metropolitan police commissioners and deputy inspectors general (DIGs) of police ranges were also present at the meeting. Additional police personnel have been ordered to be deployed in four districts—Gopalganj, Shariatpur, Madaripur and Faridpur. . A police source said that leaders and activists of the party of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina had been carrying out acts of sabotage across the country centring on her announcement that she would return to Bangladesh. Leaders who have fled abroad are instigating these activities and sending money to fund sabotage, the source added. Names of those behind the incidents have reportedly emerged during the interrogation of people recently arrested in connection with sabotage. . Officials concerned said that eight to nine crude bombs exploded at different locations of Dhaka University within a short period on Sunday evening. Three people were arrested on the spot in connection with the incidents. The arrested individuals are from Gopalganj, Rajshahi and Naogaon.
